name: Gelato Vero Caffe
notes: Router said no-platform. Restaurant's own Squarespace site (not Wix) - the /menu page's GELATO/COFFEE/ESPRESSO tab widget renders style="display:none" on the two inactive tabs, but confirmed by reading the raw HTML (not the rendered DOM) that ALL THREE tab panels are fully present server-side, so this is not the Wix active-tab-only case; all three panels were read in full. Coffee items print their size ladder as one pipe-separated string (e.g. House "$2.65 | 3.20 | 3.50 | 3.90") with no size names on the page; split into separate dish rows in ascending price order and labeled Small/Medium/Large/Extra Large as the standard cafe convention - this is a naming inference on the printed prices, not a constructed price (every number is read verbatim, none divided, averaged or invented). Iced Coffee and Cold Brew print only 3 prices each (no Small tier), labeled Medium/Large/Extra Large accordingly. Separately checked the site's other nav pages: /gelato (titled "Retail" in its own <title>) lists distinct retail scoop pricing (Small $6/Medium $7.50/Large $9) alongside slightly different pint/quart figures ($12.50 pint matches the /menu page exactly, but quart reads $19.25 here vs $19.50 on /menu - both recorded from their own pages, flagged as a same-site discrepancy rather than resolved by guessing); /caffe (titled "Caffé") describes fresh-baked pastries, chai, and gelato-espresso drinks (Verocinno Frosty, Espresso con Gelato) with no prices anywhere on the page - stripped tags confirmed zero $ figures, so these named items could not be priced and are excluded, noted as a gap; /wholesale and /flavorsandprices pages are wholesale/bulk-tub pricing for chefs and catering accounts (Gelato Tray/Tub, Sorbetto Tray/Tub) and a full flavor list - excluded as a business-to-business adjunct, not a consumer menu. Address confirmed 3753 India St., San Diego, CA 92103 on every page footer. 26 dishes across Gelato, Gelato Retail, Coffee, and Espresso. name: Panchita's Kitchen & Bakery
notes: Router said no-platform. Site is a SpotHopper website (static.spotapps.co assets) but the /food-menu page is plain server-rendered HTML with prices directly in food-price/food-item-description divs - no __NUXT__ blob needed here. Confirmed via the site's own /locations page that the work list address (3803 32nd St, San Diego, CA 92104) is the North Park location, which the site itself describes as serving 'the full food menu (Burritos, Tacos, Tortas, Salads, Plates) with a limited selection of bakery items' - exactly the content captured from /food-menu (Breakfast Burritos, Breakfast Plates, Soups or Salads, Burritos & Bowls, Savory Empanadas, Tortas, Tacos, Quesadillas, Fries & Nachos, Sides, and a short Pastries list). The site's /drink-menu URL actually renders a completely different, much larger (100+ item) Mexican bakery list explicitly labeled 'available ONLY at our Golden Hills, Barrio Logan, and City Heights locations' - a different set of branches - so that content was deliberately excluded as a wrong-branch menu, not merged in. Most items had price in a food-price div paired 1:1 with a food-item-title h3, sectioned by the preceding h2; a handful of items (Fries & Nachos' four items, and Sides' Beans/Rice/Tortillas) print their sizes and prices as plain text inside food-item-description instead (e.g. 'Small $11.50 | Large $14.50') - each read directly from its own description text and added as separate size-suffixed rows, not divided or averaged. Modifier upcharges excluded as add-ons, not standalone dishes: 'Add Carne Asada +$6.50 / Add Chicken +$4.50' (Chilaquiles, House Salad), 'Order it Oaxaca Style +$2.00' / 'Make it a Plate +$5.75' (Tacos, Quesadillas). Cent endings are .00/.25/.50/.75/.95 with no markup divisor (1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25/1.3/0.96) producing a round-number cluster. 99 dishes across Breakfast Burritos, Breakfast Plates, Soups or Salads, Burritos & Bowls, Savory Empanadas, Tortas, Tacos, Quesadillas, Fries & Nachos, Sides, Pastries. None inferred, merged, divided, or truncated.

blocked: temp-closed, reopening 2026-10-01: WebSearch/Yelp confirm 'RK SUSHI - TEMP. CLOSED' with a stated reopen date of October 1, 2026 (today is 2026-09-02). Router said no-platform; the restaurant's own site (rksushisd.com) is a single-page Squarespace site with zero prices and one ordering link (rksushia.menu11.com/sandiego/order) that now returns a bare 'NO SITE FOUND' (dead). DoorDash's listing is marked inactive ('not available on DoorDash right now' per WebSearch). Found two independently-owned priced sources instead: allmenus.com's page (footer explicitly reads 'Menu for Rk sushi provided by Allmenus.com... (c)2023 GrubHub, Inc.', confirming it is the Grubhub-family listing, 96 prices, address-confirmed 334 W Washington St) and Postmates' store page (Uber-family, __REACT_QUERY_STATE__ catalogItems, 37 prices, address-confirmed via its own FAQ block: 'Rk sushi is located at: 334 W Washington St, San Diego'). Both pass the markup test individually (Grubhub/allmenus: 95 of 96 prices end in .95, no divisor 1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25/1.3/0.96 produces a round cluster; Postmates: clean quarter-dollar endings .00/.25/.50/.75, same result) - neither looks like a delivery surcharge on its own. But they DISAGREE on overlapping items rather than confirming each other: California Roll $8.95 (allmenus) vs $7.75 (Postmates), Miso Soup $5.95 vs $3.75, Edamame $8.95 vs $6.50, Spicy Calamari $8.95 vs $10.25, with no consistent direction or divisor tying the two together. Per the rule that disagreement is information rather than a small true sample, and given the restaurant is not currently trading and has no first-party or dine-in artefact available to arbitrate which number is current, this is left blocked rather than filing either source (or an average) as the menu. Re-check after the 2026-10-01 reopen, when the restaurant's own site/ordering link may be live again.

name: Alexi's Greek Cafe
blocked: stale-pricing: no website on record (router null). Found a DoorDash store page (schema.org Menu JSON-LD, address-confirmed 3863 Fifth Ave, San Diego, CA 92103 via its own FAQ block) and an allmenus.com page (footer-confirmed Grubhub-provided) - both carry the IDENTICAL 63-item price list to the cent (Pita Bread $1.00, Coffee $1.00, Hot Chocolate $1.00, 1/4 lb. Hamburger on Bun $3.25, most sandwiches $3.95, Gyros Plate $8.99), which is not two independent confirmations but one shared/syndicated feed neither platform has refreshed. That price level is implausible for 2026 San Diego (a $1 cup of coffee, $3.95 sandwiches) and directly contradicted by a WebSearch summary citing modern figures for the same restaurant (Gyro Plate $14.50, Greek Salad $10.86, Baklava $3.60) - roughly 1.5-1.6x higher, matching the playbook's 'a 2x+ gap is staleness, not markup, the cheaper one is an old page' pattern. Could not re-locate a citable page carrying those higher figures directly: restaurantguru.com's own page (explicitly barred as an aggregator requiring independent corroboration) has no per-item prices at all, only a $10-20 per-person range; restaurantji.com likewise has no menu prices, only review-derived favorite-dish names. alexis-greek-cafe.weeblyte.com is on the barred farm-domain list and was not opened. No DoorDash-listed Uber Eats or Grubhub direct storefront URL was found within the time budget. Blocked rather than filing the stale DoorDash/allmenus price list or guessing at the higher figures found only in an unverified search summary.

Blocked rather than filing the DoorDash bag-of-beans list as the café menu.

name: Rosarito's Mexican Food
notes: Router said no-platform (site is rosaritosmexicanfood.shop). That .shop domain does not redirect elsewhere (curl -sIL returns 200 directly) but is the same mass-produced template family seen elsewhere in this batch (public/css/template/color-4.css, template/font/font-19.css) - and unlike a legitimate instance of that template, THIS restaurant's /menu page has almost no real pricing: of 112 dish-panel items in the HTML, 109 have an empty price span and only 3 (Two Asada Tacos $14.00, Two Shredded Beef Tacos $11.95, Tamal&Cheese Enchilada $11.25) carry a real price - far below the 5-priced-item floor, so that source was not used. The site's NetWaiter link (rosaritotacoshopno6.netwaiter.com) answered its GetMenu POST with the documented empty signature {"Groups":[],"ExternalType":null}, confirming a genuinely unpopulated storefront (About page only), not a fetch failure. Used DoorDash's store page instead (schema.org Menu JSON-LD, 91 items across Most Ordered, A la carte, Combinations, Specials, Burritos, Tacos, Crispy Tacos), address-confirmed via its own FAQ block: 'Rosarito's Mexican Food #6 - 14490 Olde Highway 80 is located at 14490 Olde Highway 80, El Cajon, CA 92021' - exact match to the work list, and the '#6' store-number naming is a chain-branch label, not a different business. Ran the markup test (divide by 1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25/1.3/0.96): no divisor produced a majority round-number cluster (best was 7 of 91 at 1.10), so no uniform delivery surcharge was detected, despite the prices carrying unusual non-round cents (e.g. $8.63, $17.62, $21.61) - recorded as read, not adjusted. FLAG: a separate WebSearch summary for this restaurant cited noticeably lower figures for four of the same items (Carne Asada Fries $19.54, California Burrito $16.09, Combo #4 $15.24, Breakfast Burrito $14.09) that are each consistently ~1.157x below what this fetch shows - since that summary did not cite an independent second URL (likely a stale cache of this same DoorDash page rather than a genuine second source) it was not treated as a corroborating or contradicting source per se, but is noted here as an open discrepancy worth a re-check. 'Most Ordered' carousel items that duplicated a categorized item's exact name and price (California Burrito, 3 Mini Tacos, Beans & Cheese Burrito, Carne Asada Burrito, 5 Rolled Tacos, Quesadilla & 2 Rolled Tacos, 2 Chicken Flautas) were dropped as duplicates rather than double-counted; the 5 items unique to that carousel (Carne Asada Fries, Breakfast Burrito, Agua Frescas, Cheese Quesadilla, Full Order Rice or Beans) were kept under 'Most Ordered (unique items)'. 84 dishes after dedup. None inferred, merged, divided, or truncated.
